items.what: The run-complete PUBLISH GATE has failed 3 time(s) in a row within the last 60 min -- the site/report pipeline is WEDGED and run_complete markers are piling up unpublished. Latest cause: the publish COMMIT did not land -- the publisher's OWN scoped suite was GREEN, so this is NOT a publish-path regression: the pre-commit hook chain refused the commit (most often another lane's red on the shared tree), outran the hook deadline, or the push never reached origin. Read the 'git/hook output' tail in the log -- it names the refusing gate (rc=77, git=74e9be26a). items.how: ATTRIBUTED CAUSE: `gate_refusal` -- `git commit` returned rc=1 and the pre-commit hook chain named 1 red test(s) -- recorded in .last_gate_blocking_tests.json against this same commit. BLOCKING TEST (gate subject 74e9be26a): FAILED tests/design/test_atom_records_store.py::test_declarations_match_the_store_both_directions. Run exactly that node id against a clean checkout of HEAD. 1 test(s) were named by the PRE-COMMIT HOOK CHAIN that refused the publish commit -- that is the whole red set of the hook that refused, and the hooks behind it never ran, so there may be more. Fix these TOGETHER and expect the next hook to have its own say. rc=-9 is almost certainly OOM (free memory or cut test parallelism), NOT a code bug; rc>0 means run that test at HEAD to find the regression. Full output: docs/observability/sim-runner-log.md, 'Publish gate RED output tail'. The alarm clears automatically on the next clean publish. SUSPECTS (re-derived from the blocking test above -- NOT what was filed most recently): first-party modules that test imports: tools/merge_atom_status.py, tools/simplifications_store.py, tools/maturity_map_store.py. NO commit in the last 7 days touched those paths -- so the cause is more likely environmental (memory, a stale derived artefact, a data file) than a code change. SUSPECT HIT RATE: 1/1 closed episodes where the repair touched a path this alarm had named (19 more emitted no list at all). Diagnostic only -- never a target (R12); if it stays at 0 the re-derivation is as useless as the recency list it replaced and should be said so.
